description: §19.16.6 (S430 round 3, H2 + M1) — the lowering's decision to move a nested function in front of the `try` is STRUCTURAL. (1) `show` references `a`, which a DESTRUCTURING `const { a }` declares after the defer — it stays with that binding and returns "INNER" (a name-only analysis hoisted it and it silently read the OUTER `a`). (2) `sum` references `p`/`q` from `const [p, q]` after the defer — kept with them (hoisting threw ReferenceError). (3) `helper` mentions `kind` only as an object key, inside a string and as its own shadowing local — it is NOT a reference to the tail's `kind`, so it is hoisted and callable BEFORE the defer (a text match kept it inside and it threw TypeError). trace = "INNER;D1;sum3;D2;local1kind;tail;D3;" — identical to the no-defer twin `hoist-structural-twin`.
rationale: §19.16.6: the lowering SHALL NOT change the meaning of the rest of the block — a nested function declared after the defer stays visible to the whole block, unless its body refers to a binding declared after the defer, in which case it stays with that binding. Observable result must equal the no-defer twin.
